payload.supporting_quote: Blood homocysteine is not elevated in migraine.
The homocysteine serum levels were significantly higher in migraine with aura compared to migraine without aura.
There were not any significant differences on median serum homocysteine levels between migraine with aura (8.0 mikromol/L) and without aura (8.5 mikromol/L). (p=0.426)

We found significant differences in homocysteine levels between various diagnostic groups (K-W test: p=0.005). One-way ANOVA, post-hoc tests revealed significant differences in homocysteine levels between Non-migraineurs, MWA (p=0.002, CI: 1.93 - 9.19) and MWoA (p=0.002, CI: -9.19 - -1.9).
plasma homocysteine levels were lower in MWA than in MWOA.
Meta-analysis was indicative of higher Hcy concentration in migraine patients vs HC overall [adults and children: 16 studies, I ...]
